blocks.text: OPINI - To the silly yolk, Einstein said, love is to do the same but to expect a different outcome.
80 years of free Ri. 25 years of the Reformation Era. Nine years of the Mental Revolution. The main issue remains the same, which is the availability of the main ingredients of consumption: rice.
Other countries have been talking about innovation in advanced technology. Dealing with a product that only requires primitive technology and madya, we're not done yet. And it's been decades.
And still dreaming of 2045 Indonesia Gold? It needs to be introspection.
Cultural vs Policy

The availability of rice can be seen from the perspective of the 101 principle of economics: Supply vs demand. Or the production of yeast consumption. If you have deficit or produce less than consumption, there are three ways to cover it. First, increase production plus import. Second, reduce consumption. Or, a combination of the two.
For decades, we tend to focus on production plus imports.
Per 2023, production is 34 million tons. Consumption 35.7 million tons. Deficit 1.7 million tons. With 35.7 million tons per year, that's 0.1 million tons a day.
For 27 years, I ate rice 3 times a day, 7 times a week, 365 days a year. Because of cultural and environmental factors, over the last 30 years, it's reduced drastically to one-on-one.
Humans can adapt to situations, whether it's policy, environment, or culture. It's been proven since prehistoric times.
What does it matter if there's a national movement of food diversity? Evolving movement, not the origin of jargon movements, which are basically often the meaning of moving in place.

A few years ago I said the same thing. Indonesia needs less rice consumption one day or half a day per week. It can be equivalent to not consuming rice one breakfast and one lunch a week. Replaced with groceries like yams, corn, or something. The important thing is that proteins and other nutrients don't decrease.
Without eating rice one day a week, it could reduce the consumption of 5 million tons per year. Or, without consuming rice one lunch a week, it reduces rice consumption to nearly 2 million per year.
No need to import. And there's no need to share the rice during elections. Because it's basically demeaning to the people of Indonesia.
Translations Command

It's true that rice is the main food item. However, it's hard to argue that rice is also the object of many parties' main benefits, whether it's monetary and political gain. That the primary needs became objects of profit and politics, it shows that Indonesia is not yet free. Still colonized by the interests of his nation's elite.
This is where it takes the transformation of leadership. A leader has to be smart to see constructive solutions to chronic problems, not to be late or lost in them.

A smart leader must also transform community habits or his nation to constructive and be able to answer the challenges or problems he faces. Singapore, South Korea, and Japan have shown it. Progress is built on cultural transformation.

Leaders in Indonesia, of all levels and all fields, should be able to bring change, not be part of the problem. Change in a better direction. Being a transformation agent. That's the most basic condition of being a leader.
Indonesia misses him.
Elwin Tobing, California, USA
Professor of Economics. The book is about to rise.
